q: I think cash on delivery is the reason we're losing money. Is that true?
answer:
Net profit is down slightly vs yesterday but Cash-on-Delivery (COD) is not the reason the business lost money: net profit moved from ₹3,875 on 2026-10-27 to ₹3,331 on 2026-10-28 (−14.1%), and the statistical diagnosis finds no supported causal role for COD — COD volumes rose a little while COD handling fees actually fell and the change is explained by ad spend and contribution swings instead.

What’s behind it
- Net profit: ₹3,875 → ₹3,331 (−14.1%). The day’s swing is an ordinary fluctuation within the metric’s recent range and the diagnosis found no single measured cause.
- Ad spend (P&L basis) rose sharply and dominated the bridge: ₹43,452 → ₹60,101 (+38.3%). This increase produced a negative effect on net profit larger than the net-profit change.
- Product contribution margin also rose: ₹47,327 → ₹63,432 (+34.0%), which offset some of the ad-spend hit. The net effect reconciles arithmetically to the profit change.
- COD activity: Cod orders 10 → 12 (+20.0%, within its normal range); cod handling fee ₹191 → ₹0 (fell outside its usual range). The diagnosis tests COD and reports it is ruled out as a supported cause — the raw association disappears after calendar and competing-driver adjustments.

Worth checking: why ad spend jumped (which campaigns and cost lines increased) — that is the largest actionable lever shown by the data.

Period: 2026-10-27..2026-10-28 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
